metaDesc: A hand-picked guide to Lamphun's best cafes that are actually open — old-town spots near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, quiet rice-field cafes, and northern hill coffee. With areas, prices and opening hours for easy planning in Thailand.

h1:
Best Cafes in Lamphun
Old Town, Rice Fields & Hill Coffee
intro: Lamphun is the kind of small town where you can cafe-hop all day without rushing. Visit Wat Phra That Hariphunchai in the morning, then stop at a spot in the old town; drive just a few minutes out of town in the afternoon and you'll find cafes sitting in the middle of green rice fields, quiet enough to hear the wind. We picked 10 places that are genuinely open and where locals actually go, with the area, prices and opening hours so you can plan easily.

blocks.html: Lamphun is only about 30 minutes from Chiang Mai, so plenty of people drive over for a morning-to-evening cafe day trip. The charm here is the slower pace: cafes aren't packed the way Nimman gets, and you get both old-town spots in buildings with a bit of history and rice-field cafes where you can sit watching the green for an hour. We ranked these on atmosphere, coffee quality and real reviews — not just on which place happens to be more famous.

blocks.title: How to read this ranking
blocks.html: The order reflects the overall mix (atmosphere + coffee + quiet), not a fixed verdict on which cafe is objectively best. Each one has a different strength, so pick based on whether you want old town, rice fields, or serious coffee.

items.name: Temple House Lamphun
items.blurb: A cafe right in the old town on Inthayongyot Road, a few minutes' walk from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai. It's an old house given a warm, low-key makeover, with seating both indoors and in a small garden — perfect for a stop after morning prayers. The coffee is made with care and the bakery is homemade.

items.name: SIP WHISPER
items.blurb: A newer cafe out by the rice fields, homey and surrounded by greenery and paddy. It's quiet and easy to settle into for a long morning or evening, and it's the spot people looking for a rice-field cafe in Lamphun mention most often.
items.meta: Rice fields, out of town · Open 7:30–17:00 (Mon–Thu), until 20:30 Fri–Sun

items.name: Yann
items.blurb: A vintage rooftop cafe in central Lamphun with a view over the old town. The look is relaxed and retro, there are plenty of photo corners, and it suits younger crowds and remote workers wanting a chill spot. Closed Wednesdays.

items.name: Black to Basic
items.blurb: A black, bare-concrete cafe on Chaimongkol Road near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai — coolly understated, with its own bakery recipes and a wide drinks menu. It opens early, so it's good for a stop before you head out to explore the town.
items.meta: In town, Chaimongkol Road · Open daily 07:00–17:00

items.name: View Doi
items.blurb: A garden-house cafe set in a date-palm grove around the edge of Ban Hong and Wiang Nong Long districts — fresh, shady and relaxing. The standouts are the date-palm coffee and date-palm smoothie, which are hard to find elsewhere. Good for a quieter drive a little farther out.
items.meta: Ban Hong, garden house · Open until 17:00

items.name: SUKSUD
items.blurb: A homey Japanese-style wooden-house cafe in Ban Don Luang, Mae Raeng subdistrict, Pa Sang. The draw is the homemade gelato and ice cream, starting at ฿40 a scoop. It sits in the Don Luang handwoven-cotton area, so you can pair it with a village visit.
items.meta: Pa Sang, Ban Don Luang · Open daily 09:00–17:00

items.name: Lapuné Cafe
items.blurb: A rustic Japanese-style cafe with a shady garden and lots of seating options, from cool air-conditioned rooms to camp chairs under the trees. Great if you want to sit for a long stretch with no rush.
items.meta: Out of town, garden · Indoor and outdoor seating

items.name: Malila Cafe & Restaurant
items.blurb: A clean, white-toned spot on the ring road in the moat area, no more than a 10-minute walk from Wat Phra That. It does desserts, drinks and full meals, so it's good for lingering across mealtimes. Closed Wednesdays.
items.meta: In town, moat area · Open 11:00–20:00 (closed Wed)

items.name: Hom Cafe
items.blurb: A simple, minimalist cafe not far from Wat Phra That, with a small garden corner to catch the breeze. It focuses on drinks and desserts and works well for a short break while you explore the town. Closed Mondays.
items.meta: In town, near the temple · Open 08:00–17:00 (closed Mon)

items.name: Aq Bur Old Town
items.blurb: A cafe in the old-town heart of Lamphun, just past the governor's residence on the right before the post office. Its standout is staying open until 9pm — handy if you want a late-evening cafe, which is rare in a town this small.

blocks.text: Old-town cafes within walking distance of the temple

blocks.html: If you park near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and go on foot, the old town around it has several cafes within walking distance. The charm is that you get to see the old buildings, the city wall, and Lamphun's slow rhythm of life along the way.

items: Temple House Lamphun — a renovated old house on Inthayongyot Road, the closest to the temple, ideal for a sit-down after visiting.
Black to Basic — black, bare-concrete on Chaimongkol Road, opens early for a coffee before you explore.
Aq Bur Old Town — open until 9pm, your go-to for an evening cafe in town.
Malila / Hom Cafe — in the moat area, under a 10-minute walk from the temple, good for lingering.

blocks.title: Old-town tip
blocks.html: Several old-town cafes have a weekly day off (for example closed Wednesdays or Mondays). Check the hours on the cafe's page before you set out, especially if you're coming mid-week, so you don't make the trip for nothing.

blocks.text: Rice-field cafes: quiet spots out of town

blocks.html: One thing Lamphun still has that's getting harder to find in Chiang Mai is cafes in the middle of the rice fields that are genuinely quiet. Drive just over ten minutes out toward Pa Sang or Ban Hong and you'll find spots where you can sit looking at green paddy without the crowds. The fields are at their greenest from the rainy season into early cool season (June–November).

items.name: SIP WHISPER
items.blurb: A homey rice-field cafe surrounded by trees and paddy — quiet and easy, ideal for a long morning or evening.

items.name: View Doi (Ban Hong)
items.blurb: A garden house in a date-palm grove with a hard-to-find date-palm coffee, good for a peaceful drive farther out.

items.name: Lapuné Cafe
items.blurb: A rustic Japanese-style garden with camp chairs under the trees, where you can catch the breeze all day.

blocks.text: On hill coffee and the quiet

blocks.html: Lamphun doesn't grow as much of its own coffee as the hills around Chiang Mai, but plenty of cafes here use northern hill beans (Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai) that they roast and brew themselves. If you take your coffee seriously, try a pour-over or espresso to taste the bean. And if you're after quiet, the out-of-town spots — rice-field or garden cafes — deliver it better than in-town places on weekends.

items: Want serious coffee — pick in-town cafes that focus on coffee, like Temple House and Black to Basic.
Want quiet — head out of town to the rice fields or garden cafes, like SIP WHISPER, View Doi and Lapuné.
Want dessert / ice cream — SUKSUD (homemade gelato) or Malila, which has a big sweets menu.

blocks.title: When the fields are green
blocks.html: If you want photos of bright-green paddy, come from the rainy season into early cool season (around June–November). After the harvest the fields are left as stubble and the scene looks different, so it's worth checking the timing with the cafe's page first.

faq.q: Which old-town cafes in Lamphun are near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai?
faq.a: Several are within easy walking distance of Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, including Temple House Lamphun on Inthayongyot Road, Black to Basic on Chaimongkol Road, plus Malila and Hom Cafe in the moat area, under a 10-minute walk away. Aq Bur Old Town stays open until 9pm, which is good for an evening sit-down.

faq.q: Are there any quiet rice-field cafes to recommend in Lamphun?
faq.a: The standouts are SIP WHISPER, a rice-field cafe surrounded by trees and paddy; View Doi, a garden-house cafe in a date-palm grove around Ban Hong; and Lapuné Cafe, a rustic Japanese-style garden. All are out of town and quieter than in-town spots on weekends.

faq.q: When are Lamphun's rice fields greenest for photos at rice-field cafes?
faq.a: The fields are at their greenest from the rainy season into early cool season, roughly June to November. After the harvest they turn to stubble and the scene changes, so it's best to check the timing with the cafe's page before you go.

faq.q: Roughly how much does coffee cost at Lamphun cafes?
faq.a: Most coffee and drinks run around ฿50–80 a cup, a little cheaper than cafes in Chiang Mai. Desserts like the gelato at SUKSUD start at ฿40 a scoop.

faq.q: Is it easy to visit Lamphun cafes from Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Yes. Lamphun is only about 30 minutes from Chiang Mai by car, and many people drive over for a morning-to-evening cafe day trip. Having your own car is easiest, since several rice-field cafes are out of town and hard to reach by public transport.
